dedupe_keys.name: sri lanka disaster management centre situation reports about 4 900 daily and event reports with affected families and people damaged houses damage to critical infrastructure and safety centres by district

description: Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre issues situation reports whenever floods, landslides, storms, droughts or other hazards affect the country, and keeps them all online. The archive holds about 4,900 reports, with the latest dated 24 September 2026, plus a separate series of drought situation reports. Each report is a trilingual table, in Sinhala, Tamil and English, listing by district and divisional secretariat the families and people affected, houses fully and partly damaged, damage to small and medium enterprises, damage to critical infrastructure, and the number of safety centres open and the people sheltering in them. Coverage is national. The reports are free and available to download as PDF from the DMC site; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: figures are provisional counts compiled during events and revised in later reports, the tables must be extracted from PDF, and the report list does not tag the hazard type in a structured way. Simulation uses: building event histories of disaster impacts by district, calibrating evacuation and shelter demand models, and checking exposure models of housing and infrastructure against observed damage. Related records: the Copernicus EMS on-demand mapping (data-copernicus-ems-on-demand-mapping) maps some of the same events, and the Taiwan disaster case data (data-nfa-taiwan-disaster-case-data) are a comparable national event record.
